national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 81 India Emerging as Trusted Partner in Global Semiconductor Industry: Ashwini Vaishnaw
national_raw_news.content: Electronics and Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw today said India is emerging as a trusted partner in the global semiconductor industry. Participating at a fireside chat at Semicon India 2026 in New Delhi, Mr. Vaishnaw said trust is crucial in the semiconductor industry, from protecting intellectual property to enabling global companies to design end-to-end products in India. He said trusted supply chains could become one of India’s key strengths. Mr. Vaishnaw said India had set a target of training 85 thousand semiconductor design engineers over ten years. He said 70 thousand have already been trained in four years. The Minister said students across the country are now designing and taping out chips. Around 400 engineering colleges have access to industry-grade Electronic Design Automation tools. Mr. Vaishnaw said India needs a clear 20-year roadmap for the semiconductor sector. He said the industry is among the world’s most complex. India’s approach is to build a strong foundation for sustained and long-term growth. He said the India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 (Semicon 2.0) focuses on six key areas. These include chip design, materials, fabrication, Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging, or ATMP, research and development, and storage. Later, talking to the media, Mr Vaishnaw said around 30 companies from one country are participating across the pavilions at Semicon India. He said students have also shown strong enthusiasm and curiosity. The Minister said the semiconductor sector is expected to generate more than one lakh jobs. Several MoUs were also exchanged and new collaborations announced at Semicon India 2026 in the presence of Mr Vaishnaw. The initiatives aim to strengthen India’s semiconductor ecosystem. Mr. Vaishnaw and Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi also inaugurated the Odisha Pavilion at the event.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 91 Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan Highlights Yoga’s Role in Physical and Mental Well-Being
national_raw_news.content: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan today said yoga can help improve physical and mental well-being, concentration, self-awareness and mental balance amid the growing stress of modern life. The Vice President was addressing the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of the Gordhandas Seksaria College of Yoga and Cultural Synthesis at Kaivalyadhama at Lonavala in Maharashtra. Mr. Radhakrishnan appreciated the institution’s 75-year contribution to yoga education, research and cultural studies. He said Kaivalyadhama founder Swami Kuvalayananda laid the foundation for the scientific study of yoga in 1924. He said yoga is not merely a tradition of one generation. He described it as a heritage that must be preserved for future generations. He said yoga has gained global recognition through Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s initiatives and the United Nations’ declaration of 21st of June as the International Day of Yoga. The Vice President said true progress means embracing modern technology and development while preserving good traditions and accepting appropriate changes. He urged students to bring the values learned through yoga into their daily lives. These include discipline, concentration, patience and self-awareness. Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma, former Union Minister and Chairman of Kaivalyadhama Global Suresh Prabhu, CEO Subodh Tiwari, teachers, staff and students were present on the occasion.

national_raw_news.title: India, Nepal discuss measures to facilitate greater market access for products of both countries 7 hours ago 105
national_raw_news.content: India and Nepal discussed measures to facilitate greater market access for products of both countries. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry in a statement said that during the two day meeting of Inter-Governmental Sub-Committee (IGSC) on Trade, Transit and Cooperation to Control Unauthorised Trade which concluded yesterday both sides reviewed a wide range of issues. It was related to market access, Customs and trade facilitation, standards, food safety, border infrastructure, rail and road connectivity and other trade-related matters. The Indian delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Department of Commerce, Ujjwal Kumar Ghosh, while the Nepali delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Buddha Bahadur Gurung. The meeting focused on facilitating legitimate trade while strengthening mechanisms to ensure compliance with applicable rules and prevent misuse of preferential trade arrangements. Both sides also reviewed rail and road connectivity, movement of freight, Integrated Check Posts and land-port infrastructure. The discussions focused on improving the utilisation of existing infrastructure and addressing operational bottlenecks affecting bilateral and transit trade. The Ministry said that India and Nepal share close historical, cultural and economic ties and the discussions at the IGSC are expected to further strengthen bilateral trade, transit connectivity and economic cooperation between the two countries.

national_raw_news.content: JP Nadda reviews health sector progress in Madhya Pradesh; commends state’s healthcare expansion and PPP model Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर JP Nadda reviews health sector progress in Madhya Pradesh; commends state’s healthcare expansion and PPP model ANI | Updated: Sep 18, 2026 21:59 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 18 (ANI): Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare JP Nadda met Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Friday to review the progress of the health sector in the State, with discussions focusing on healthcare infrastructure, medical education, specialised services and key public health initiatives. According to an official release, during the meeting, Nadda appreciated the Madhya Pradesh Government for its sustained efforts to strengthen the State’s healthcare ecosystem and expand access to quality healthcare. He particularly commended the State for leveraging the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model to accelerate the expansion of medical education and healthcare infrastructure. A key focus of the review was the expansion of medical education in the State. Madhya Pradesh has increased its MBBS seats from 5,600 to 6,120 in 2026, adding 520 seats in a year. The State has also expanded super-speciality education, with seats in government medical colleges increasing from 63 to 73, and in private medical colleges from 29 to 53, the release mentioned. According to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Nadda appreciated these efforts, emphasising that expansion of medical education and specialist capacity will strengthen the healthcare workforce and improve the availability of advanced healthcare services across the State. The Union Health Minister also lauded Madhya Pradesh for its innovative use of the PPP model for establishing medical colleges. Under the initiative, medical colleges are being established in Dhar, Panna, Katni and Betul, with the institutions targeted for establishment by December 2027. The initiative represents an important step towards expanding medical education and bringing specialised healthcare services closer to people across different regions of the State. Nadda appreciated the State Government’s approach of combining public investment with private-sector participation to augment healthcare capacity and accelerate infrastructure development. The meeting also reviewed improvements in key maternal and child health indicators. As per SRS 2022–24, Madhya Pradesh’s Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) declined by 7 points to 135 per lakh live births. The proportion of pregnant women receiving four or more ANC visits increased from 57.5% to 69.5%, as per NFHS-6. Child health indicators have also shown improvement, with the Neonatal Mortality Rate declining from 27 to 26 and the Infant Mortality Rate from 37 to 35 per 1,000 live births. The State has also strengthened access to specialised healthcare. 70 haemodialysis units are operational across 52 districts, while 52 cancer day-care centres are providing cancer treatment services. Advanced cancer treatment facilities, including CAR-T cell therapy, have also been introduced at Government Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Medical College, Indore. The expansion of medical education infrastructure is further supported by new government medical colleges.
